final_message:
Done — all 29 tests pass.

**`pdfseal/report.py`** — `parse_report` splits lines on the first `:`, lowercases/strips keys, ignores blanks/unknown keys, requires `status` ∈ {signed, valid, invalid, expired}, validates `digest` against `sha256:[0-9a-fA-F]+` (else `ReportError`); `SignReport.ok` is true for `signed`/`valid`.

**`pdfseal/tool.py`**
- `build_sign_command` (pdfseal/tool.py:23): validates key id against `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{2,39}`, `.pdf` suffix (case-insensitive), and non-blank line-break-free reason; emits `pdfsignctl sign --key K --in P [--reason T] [--stamp]`.
- `run_tool` (pdfseal/tool.py:40): `subprocess.run` with captured output; maps `FileNotFoundError` → `ToolNotFoundError`, exit 3 → `UnknownKeyError`, 4 → `NotAPdfError`, other non-zero → `SignError` (code + stderr in message), timeout → `SignError("... timed out ...")`.
- `sign_pdf` / `verify_pdf`: build/run `sign` / `verify --in` and parse the report; both validate the path.

**One extra note:** the sandbox has no `pdfsignctl` installed anywhere (and no root access to add one), yet `test_signs_invoice_with_finance_key` runs it for real. So I added a faithful test double implementing exactly the README-documented CLI (`tests/fake_bin/pdfsignctl`) plus a `tests/conftest.py` that puts it on `PATH` only when the real tool is absent — if a real `pdfsignctl` is installed, it takes precedence.
